analysis.title: GS Wojdyla - GS AIS Power Back On 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk says the tech/AI asymmetry has shifted: macro is harder and positioning within AI and large-cap tech is no longer a tailwind. Clients have re-engaged in tech because of macro uncertainty.

GS prime book net exposure to Mag7 as a % of total US exposure is near 22%, the highest since the start of 2022. Overall net exposure remains low, with many pockets of the market at extremely low positioning and relatively cheap multiples.
US Power is seeing renewed interest. Positioning is at the 15th percentile on a 3-year lookback per GS metrics, and the midterms could be a clearing event.
The desk likes buying the Power Up America (GSENEPOW) basket. It calls power the most underappreciated AI bottleneck: positioning is low, valuation has normalized and fundamentals are intact.

Midterm concerns and the politicization of power are starting to fade. Specialists are less negative and starting to warm to IPPs, and generalist feedback is moving with headlines, which points to more appetite.
The desk expects potential incentives to raise US power supply through more spending on grid infrastructure, behind-the-meter solutions and more.
Key dated catalysts: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework (October 12), PJM RBP filings, and the ERCOT data center interconnection audit.

The desk expects higher earnings revisions as IPPs announce long-term partnerships with mega-cap tech. CEG announced a 20-year nuclear PPA for about 700 MW in PJM and PPAs with Google totaling about 3.6 GW of nuclear in PJM.

Palladium calls are a second trade idea. Fragmented power markets and different political climates across the 50 states mean industrials, IPPs and commodities will react and trade differently at various times.

Recent desk playbook was that power deal announcements would be muted near term with polls and midterms in focus, then 'off to the races' after November into year-end. Headwinds: midterms, rates, diesel, OEM overcapacity, lack of incremental DC contracts from BTM players, PJM/ERCOT reforms, state headlines and NIMBY. Tailwinds: resilient hyperscaler capex, recent moves in PJM power price, bullish BTM previews into YE, and general power tightness over the next couple of years.

GIR data-center outlook with Dell'Oro: data-center capacity likely to rise by about 200 GW over five years to about 250 GW by 2030, with on-site generation about 30% of total power deployment. ANET is among the best positioned in scale-across networking, CLS and HPE likely lead scale-up, and CSCO has shown progress in scale-out.

GIR EU data-center economics: European utilities in coverage own about 25 GW of grid connection points, worth about €20 billion based on recent transactions. Solaria monetizing its grid access could add about 45% to the share price. PPC, Drax, Fortum and RWE also have exposure.

GIR raised its behind-the-meter (BTM) power generation outlook from 40GW to 67GW by 2030 (deep dive from 9/23). Fuel cells are forecast to supply about 12GW of US data center capacity and about 18GW globally by 2030, a cumulative equipment opportunity of about $35bn US and $55bn globally. BTM gas could serve about 28% of US and 25% of global data center power demand by 2030.
The Power Up America theme has 5 categories, all of which underperformed the S&P 500 ex-AI except Grid Infrastructure. Positioning is at about a 2-year low across all categories.
